items.from: ### The tip of the red giant branch, at three reports
items.sentence: 67.4 ± 0.5 from an early observing and 73.04 ± 1.04 from a late one, in kilometres per second per megaparsec, five standard deviations apart; a red-giant-tip calibration of 69.6 ± 0.8 ± 1.7 between them.
items.text: Three reports of the Hubble constant from the tip of the red giant branch joined to supernovae give 69.8 ± 0.8 (statistical) ± 1.7 (systematic), 69.6 ± 0.8 ± 1.7 and 69.8 ± 0.6 ± 1.6 kilometres a second per megaparsec, the latest giving the first two together as 69.6 ± 1.9 and finding "No statistically significant difference" between its value and the one from the cosmic microwave background.
